text:
Tom Wilson's season so far is a lot of hitting and not much scoring. He leads into late November with 56 hits, a fight with Sam Carrick off the opening faceoff in Buffalo on Nov. 19, and just three goals in 22 games, the third of which ended a drought against Boston on Nov. 21. For a player who put up 62 points last season, eight points is a jarring number.

We'd bet on the chances over the drought, as a description rather than a forecast. He has 3 goals on 6.1 expected (the quality of his looks), he's shooting 7.7% against a career that sits much higher, and Washington still gets 54% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on. He's getting no power-play points at all, which is part of the gap.

Evolving-Hockey's read on last season is the reminder of what he is when it goes in: 1.9 wins above replacement, 90th percentile at driving play and 99th at taking chances away. Watch the power-play role and the shooting percentage; both have room to climb.
